claim: SpyCas9, along with a programmable single-guide RNA (sgRNA), has been exploited as a significant genome-editing tool.
source: The CRISPR-associated endonuclease Cas9 from Streptococcus pyogenes (SpyCas9), along with a programmable single-guide RNA (sgRNA), has been exploited as a significant genome-editing tool.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Two magnesium (Mg2+) ion-dependent nuclease domains (HNH and RuvC domains) in Cas9 cleave the target DNA strand (tDNA) and the non-target DNA strand (ntDNA), respectively.
source: Two, magnesium (Mg2+) ion-dependent, nuclease domains (i.e. HNH and RuvC domains) in Cas9 cleave the target DNA strand (tDNA) complementary to the guide region of a dual single-guide RNA (sgRNA) and the non-target DNA strand (ntDNA), respectively (Gasiunas et al., 2012; Jinek et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Gasiunas et al., 2012; Jinek et al., 2012).

claim: The HNH domain employs the catalytic triad of D839-H840-N863 for cleavage catalysis.
source: In this catalysis model, the HNH employs the catalytic triad of D839-H840-N863 for cleavage catalysis, rather than previously implicated D839-H840-D861, D837-D839-H840, or D839-H840-D861-N863.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling and experimental validation presented in the manuscript.

claim: The amino acid residue D861 in the HNH domain of SpyCas9 pointed towards the catalytic center in the absolute majority of resolved crystal structures.
source: Notably, the amino acid residue D861 in the HNH domain of SpyCas9 pointed towards the catalytic center in the absolute majority of resolved crystal structures (Anders et al., 2016; Anders et al., 2014; Dong et al., 2017; Hirano et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2016; Jinek et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2019; Nishimasu et al., 2014; Olieric et al., 2016; Yang and Patel, 2017), molecular dynamic simulation models (Palermo et al., 2018; Zuo and Liu, 2017), and cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures (Huai et al., 2017; Jiang et al., 2019; Shin et al., 2017) (Figure 1a–1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to structural studies and reference to Figure 1a-1d.

claim: D861 is generally believed to directly participate in Mg2+ chelation and tDNA cleavage, despite lacking experimental evidence.
source: Despite lacking experimental evidence, it is generally believed that D861 directly participates in Mg2+ chelation and tDNA cleavage (Huai et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2018; Palermo et al., 2017; Zuo and Liu, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior computational studies.

claim: The residues spatially equivalent to the D861 of SpyCas9 are conserved as an asparagine in diverse homologous structures of DNA/RNA nucleases from other species.
source: In the diverse homologous structures of DNA/RNA nucleases from other species (Yang, 2008; Yang, 2011), however, the residues spatially equivalent to the D861 of SpyCas9 are conserved as an asparagine.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies of homologous nucleases.

claim: The substitution (N62D) of the corresponding asparagine in the active center of bacteriophage T4 Endonuclease VII (T4 Endo VII) has been shown to abrogate its DNA cleavage activity.
source: The substitution (N62D) of the corresponding asparagine in the active center of bacteriophage T4 Endonuclease VII (T4 Endo VII) has been shown to abrogate its DNA cleavage activity (Biertümpfel et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to experimental work on T4 Endo VII.

claim: The D861A variant of Cas9 exhibited DNA-cleavage activity level similar to that of the wild-type protein in cell-based assays.
source: Unexpectedly, this Cas9 variant exhibited DNA-cleavage activity level similar to that of the wild-type protein (Figure 1e and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The D861 variant retained similar activity as the wild type in in vitro cleavage assays using either plasmid or oligo DNA as a substrate, given enough reaction time.
source: To further validate our finding, we performed in vitro cleavage assays using either plasmid or oligo DNA as a substrate and observed that the D861 variant retained similar activity as the wild type, given enough reaction time (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: D861 is not critical for HNH domain-catalyzed tDNA cleavage.
source: Our experiments thus demonstrate that D861 is not critical for HNH domain-catalyzed tDNA cleavage, unlike what would be expected from the reported Cas9 complex structures (Anders et al., 2014; Huai et al., 2017; Jiang et al., 2016; Palermo et al., 2018; Palermo et al., 2017; Zuo and Liu, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell-based and in vitro assays.

claim: The previously reported structures of the HNH domain of DNA-bound Cas9 potentially represent a conformation that is incompetent for tDNA cleavage.
source: In other words, the previously reported structures of the HNH domain of DNA-bound Cas9 (Huai et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2018; Palermo et al., 2017; Zuo and Liu, 2017) potentially represent a conformation that is incompetent for tDNA cleavage.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental finding that D861 is not critical for catalysis, contradicting the structural models.

claim: In the apo-state crystal structure of Cas9, the α-helical element in the HNH domain ββα-metal (ββα-Me) fold appears to pose a unique conformation with N863 pointing toward the catalytic center.
source: One noticeable feature in this apo-Cas9 structure is that the α-helical element in the HNH domain ββα-metal (ββα-Me) fold appears to pose a unique conformation with N863 pointing toward the catalytic center (Figure 1—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of the apo-Cas9 crystal structure (Jinek et al., 2014) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4a.

claim: The N-terminal of the α-helical segment is disordered in the apo-Cas9 structure, suggesting a high conformational flexibility around this region.
source: However, the N-terminal of the α-helical segment is disordered in this apo-Cas9 structure (Figure 1—figure supplement 4a), suggesting a high conformational flexibility around this region.
evidence: This claim is based on structural observation from the apo-Cas9 crystal structure.

claim: In the MD simulation of the completed apo-Cas9 structure with a Mg2+ ion, the Mg2+ ion formed an octahedral coordination with D839, N863, and four water molecules.
source: As a result, the Mg2+ ion formed an octahedral coordination with D839, N863, and four water molecules (Figure 1—figure supplement 4c), which closely resembled the Mg2+ coordination in the X-ray crystal structure of Actinomyces naeslundii Cas9 (AnaCas9, Figure 1—figure supplement 5a) (Jinek et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4c and comparison to AnaCas9 structure.

claim: In the final structure model, D839, H840 and N863 on the ββα-Me motif formed the catalytic triad that was poised for cleaving the tDNA.
source: In our final structure, D839, H840 and N863 on the ββα-Me motif formed the catalytic triad that was poised for cleaving the tDNA.
evidence: This claim is based on the computational model derived from MD simulations.

claim: The Mg2+ ion was coordinated with the residues D839 and N863 of SpyCas9, a scissile phosphate (the pro-Sp oxygen and leaving O3' engaged), and two water molecules in a strained geometry.
source: The Mg2+ ion was coordinated with the residues D839 and N863 of SpyCas9, a scissile phosphate (the pro-Sp oxygen and leaving O3' engaged), and two water molecules in a strained geometry (Figure 2d–2e).
evidence: This claim is based on the computational model shown in Figure 2d-2e.

claim: The active Cas9 structure highly resembled the catalytic configuration present in the X-ray structure of T4 Endo VII/DNA complex.
source: This structure highly resembled the catalytic configuration present in the X-ray structure of T4 Endo VII/DNA complex (Biertümpfel et al., 2007) (Figure 2c), indicating the N863 of Cas9 could be engaged in the formation of the catalytic center for tDNA cleavage.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison to T4 Endo VII shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Both SpyCas9 N863A variant and D861A/N863A double-mutant variant virtually lost the entire gene-editing capability compared to the wild-type protein in cell-based assays.
source: Both SpyCas9 variants virtually lost the entire gene-editing capability compared to the wild-type protein (Figure 1f and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The N863A variant effectively lost tDNA cleavage activity in in vitro assays, essentially producing only nicked products in the plasmid cleavage assay.
source: Consistently, our in vitro assays also showed an effective loss of tDNA cleavage activity for the N863A variant, essentially producing only nicked products in the plasmid cleavage assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and causing the disappearance of the 23-nucleotide tDNA cleavage product in the oligo assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: N863, instead of D861, is the functional catalytic residue.
source: Together, our results clearly show N863, instead of D861, is the functional catalytic residue.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mutagenesis studies.

claim: The D839A mutation substantially compromised the gene-editing activity of Cas9.
source: Here, we discovered that the D839A mutation substantially compromised the gene-editing activity of Cas9 (Figure 1f), which is consistent with our simulation studies (Zuo and Liu, 2017) and directly supports the significance of D839 for Cas9 activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f and prior simulation studies.

claim: D839, H840 and N863 are essential for the cleavage function of the HNH domain.
source: Collectively, our structural and functional data corroborate the essence of D839, H840 and N863 for the cleavage function of the HNH domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental and computational data presented in the manuscript.

claim: MD simulations excluded the likelihood of D837 and N854 to function as the catalytic residues directly engaged in the coordination of the Mg2+ ion.
source: Our MD simulations also excluded the likelihood of D837 and N854 (at the two ends of the β-sheet of the ββα-Me motif) to function as the catalytic residues previously postulated to be directly engaged in the coordination of the Mg2+ ion (Chen and Doudna, 2017b; Huai et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is based on MD simulation results.

claim: The side chain of N854 is ~10 Å distant from the tDNA, making it unlikely to be a residue that directly mediates catalysis.
source: The simulations showed that the side chain of N854 is ~10 Å distant from the tDNA, making it unlikely be a residue that directly mediates catalysis.
evidence: This claim is based on MD simulation results.

claim: N854 may play an auxiliary role in catalysis by stabilizing the activated conformation of the HNH domain through intra-molecular hydrogen bonds within the ββα-Me motif.
source: However, an activity assay demonstrated the partial loss of activity in the N854A variant (Nishimasu et al., 2014), suggesting that N854 may play an auxiliary role in catalysis. According to our MD models and the solved Cas9 structures (Figure 1a–1d), N854 may stabilize the activated conformation of the HNH domain by making several intra-molecular hydrogen bonds within the ββα-Me motif.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data from prior work and structural analysis from MD models.

claim: The D837A Cas9 moderately lost gene-editing activity.
source: The D837A Cas9 moderately lost gene-editing activity (Figure 1f).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: D837 may contribute to the structural integrity of the ββα-Me motif.
source: From the solved Cas9 structures and our simulations, D837 may contribute to the structural integrity of the ββα-Me motif, although only one hydrogen bond involving its carboxyl group appear to be established (Figure 1a–1d).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis from solved structures and MD simulations.

claim: In the pseudoactive conformation, R864 appeared to stabilize the catalytic core by forming ionic and hydrogen-bonding interactions within the ββα-Me motif.
source: In the pseudoactive conformation, R864 appeared to stabilize the catalytic core by forming ionic and hydrogen-bonding interactions within the ββα-Me motif (Figure 2a), as observed in various bound forms of Cas9 (Figure 1a–1d), whereas K866 is engaged to E371 to form a salt bridge (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2a and Figure 2b.

claim: In the active state, the corresponding residue of R864 is surrogated by K866.
source: In contrast, the corresponding residue of R864 is surrogated by K866 in the active state (Figure 2d), which is in line with the structures of AnaCas9 (K609) and SauCas9 (K583) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5), while R864, on the other hand, is tethered to a negative pocket lined by E370, E396 and D406 on the REC1 domain (Figure 2e).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2d and Figure 2e, and comparison to other Cas9 orthologs.

claim: A basic amino acid residue (Lys/Arg) seemed to be required at the catalytic core for the ββα-Me superfamily.
source: Therefore, a basic amino acid residue (Lys/Arg) seemed to be required at the catalytic core for the ββα-Me superfamily.
evidence: This claim is inferred from structural and sequence analysis across the ββα-Me nuclease superfamily.

claim: The removal of the interfacial Mg2+ ion from the models substantially destabilized the pseudoactive and active conformations of the Cas9-nucleic acid complex by ~600 kcal/mol.
source: The removal of the interfacial Mg2+ ion from our models substantially destabilized the pseudoactive and active conformations of the Cas9-nucleic acid complex by ~600 kcal/mol (Supplementary file 1), supporting the indispensable role of the Mg2+ ion for Cas9 conformational activation that has been previously demonstrated (Dagdas et al., 2017; Osuka et al., 2018; Zuo and Liu, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational free energy calculations and prior experimental work.

claim: The pseudoactive conformation (N863-OUT) appeared to be unique to SpyCas9 since the corresponding asparagine residues in other ββα-Me nucleases typically oriented toward the catalytic center.
source: The pseudoactive conformation (denoted as N863-OUT hereafter) appeared to be unique to SpyCas9 since the corresponding asparagine residues in other ββα-Me nucleases, regardless of the apo or bound form, typically oriented toward the catalytic center (Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is based on structural comparison across ββα-Me nucleases shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: End-state free energy calculations revealed that the N863-OUT SpyCas9 complex is thermodynamically more stable than its catalytically active (N863-IN) form.
source: End-state free energy calculations revealed that the N863-OUT SpyCas9 complex is thermodynamically more stable than its catalytically active (N863-IN) form (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational free energy calculations.

claim: Long time-scale MD simulations based on the isolated HNH domain of Cas9 showed that the N863-IN conformation is remarkably flexible and tends to transition to the N863-OUT conformation, but not vice versa.
source: Long time-scale MD simulations based on the isolated HNH domain of Cas9 also showed that the N863-IN conformation is remarkably flexible and tends to transition to the N863-OUT conformation, but not vice versa (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The metal centers shown in the MD-derived models were optimized by DFTB3 QM/MM simulations and showed very limited differences compared to MD simulations.
source: The metal centers shown in Figure 2a and d were optimized by DFTB3 QM/MM simulations (Figure 2—figure supplement 6). Compared to our MD simulations, we identified very limited differences from the QM/MD simulations in terms of the active site configuration.
evidence: This claim is supported by QM/MM simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: The binding of DNA to Cas9-sgRNA induces the interconversion of the HNH domain between the checkpoint intermediate (I) state and the pre-cleavage (P) state.
source: The binding of DNA to Cas9-sgRNA induces the interconversion of the HNH domain between the checkpoint intermediate (I) state and the pre-cleavage (P) state.
evidence: This claim is part of the proposed working model based on findings in this study and prior work.

claim: The ambient Mg2+ ion facilitates a conformational change to transition the HNH domain from the P state to the tDNA docked pseudoactive (D, N863-OUT) or active (D*, N863-IN) state.
source: By bridging a gap between the catalytic center and the opposite scissile phosphate, the ambient Mg2+ ion subsequently facilitates a conformational change to transition the HNH domain from the P state to the tDNA docked pseudoactive (D, N863-OUT) or active (D*, N863-IN) state.
evidence: This claim is part of the proposed working model based on findings in this study.

claim: Before the cleavage reaction occurs, both pseudoactive and active states exist and the conformational population of the two states reaches an equilibrium.
source: Before the cleavage reaction occurs, both states exist and the conformational population of the two states reaches an equilibrium.
evidence: This claim is part of the proposed working model based on findings in this study.

claim: The lower-energy pseudoactive state has larger conformational population than the active state.
source: The lower-energy pseudoactive state has larger conformational population than the active state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the free energy calculations showing the pseudoactive state is more stable.

claim: The coexistence of multiple Cas9 ternary complexes has important implications for deciphering the biphasic kinetics of Cas9-catalyzed DNA cleavage.
source: The coexistence of multiple Cas9 ternary complexes has important implications for deciphering the biphasic kinetics of Cas9-catalyzed DNA cleavage that has been shown recently by Raper et al. (2018).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the proposed model and relates to prior experimental observations.

claim: The early, fast phase of DNA cleavage characterizes a direct transition from the precatalytic state to the active state, while the slow transition from the pseudoactive to the active state likely contributes to the late, slow phase.
source: Taking their results into considerations, we surmise that the early, fast phase characterizes a direct transition from the precatalytic state to the active state, while the slow transition from the pseudoactive to the active state likely contributes to the late, slow phase.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on integrating the proposed model with prior kinetic observations.

claim: The HNH domain in multiple crystal structures remained in the N863-OUT conformation even though as high as eight Mg2+ ions were cocrystalized.
source: Consistently, the HNH domain in 4UN3 (Figure 1b, right panel) and other crystals (like 5B2R, 5B2T, 5B2S, 5FQ5, 5FW1, 5FW2, 5FW3 and 6AI6) remained in the N863-OUT conformation even though as high as eight Mg2+ ions were cocrystalized (Anders et al., 2016; Hirano et al., 2016; Nishimasu et al., 2014; Olieric et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of multiple crystal structures.

claim: The presence of metal ions alone appears to be insufficient for the HNH domain conformational activation.
source: Therefore, the presence of metal ions alone appears to be insufficient for the HNH domain conformational activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from simulation results and structural observations.

claim: SpyCas9D861A has a similar activity profile as SpyCas9WT, except for a slower rate.
source: The results indicate that SpyCas9D861A has a similar activity profile as SpyCas9WT, expect for a slower rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro cleavage assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SpyCas9N863A produces only nicked products even after one hour of reaction.
source: SpyCas9N863A produces only nicked products even after one hour of reaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro cleavage assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SpyCas9N863A lacks T-strand cleavage product, suggesting that the HNH activity is eliminated in this variant.
source: SpyCas9N863A lacks T-strand cleavage product, suggesting that the HNH activity is eliminated in this variant.
evidence: This claim is supported by oligo DNA cleavage assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: N863 is indispensable for the HNH nuclease activity.
source: In summary, our in vitro cleavage reactions of plasmid and oligo DNAs clearly indicate that N863 is indispensable for the HNH nuclease activity, whereas D861 appears to provide a supporting role to enable a faster reaction rate but is nonessential for target DNA strand cleavage.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro cleavage assay data.

claim: D861 appears to provide a supporting role to enable a faster reaction rate but is nonessential for target DNA strand cleavage.
source: In summary, our in vitro cleavage reactions of plasmid and oligo DNAs clearly indicate that N863 is indispensable for the HNH nuclease activity, whereas D861 appears to provide a supporting role to enable a faster reaction rate but is nonessential for target DNA strand cleavage.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro cleavage assay data.

claim: D861 might have a role in stabilizing the catalytic ββα-Me motif by forming an intra-molecular salt bridge.
source: A close inspection of our simulation trajectories led us to propose that D861 might have a role in stabilizing the catalytic ββα-Me motif by forming an intra-molecular salt bridge (Figure 2d), or aid initial recruitment of metal ions around the active center with other negative species like D839 and D837 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of MD simulation trajectories.

claim: D861 might aid initial recruitment of metal ions around the active center with other negative species like D839 and D837.
source: A close inspection of our simulation trajectories led us to propose that D861 might have a role in stabilizing the catalytic ββα-Me motif by forming an intra-molecular salt bridge (Figure 2d), or aid initial recruitment of metal ions around the active center with other negative species like D839 and D837 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of MD simulation trajectories.
